title: memzero_explicit throughout: correct FIPS 140-3 key zeroization discipline
description: src/cdev/crypto2dev_fd.c — memzero_explicit() is used consistently throughout: inbuf_clear(), outbuf zeroization in fd_release(), ioctl struct zeroization in ioctl_init/do_sign/do_verify/do_agree/do_kdf (on all exit paths including error paths). This is correct: the C compiler is permitted to elide a plain memset() when the buffer goes out of scope if it can prove the value is never read again. memzero_explicit() is a compiler barrier that prevents this optimization. A reviewer might suggest memset() is 'simpler' or 'equivalent' — it is not. FIPS 140-3 requires CSPs to be zeroized before memory is released; an elided memset() is a compliance failure. This is not a style preference.
